key: One of the two women said: O my father! Hire him! For the best (man) that thou canst hire in the strong, the trustworthy.
s: Moses, having watered two women’s flocks, now stands before their aged father; the Jalalayn, on 28:26, explains the strength and trust by what she told her father, his lifting the well’s stone and bidding her walk behind him.
src: The Jalalayn, Tafsīr al-Jalālayn (al-Mahalli), on 28:26, Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

evidence.words: ﴿إنّ خَيْر مَن اسْتَأْجَرْت القَوِيّ الأَمِين﴾ أيْ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ لِقُوَّتِهِ وأَمانَته فَسَأَلَها عَنْهُ فَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِما تَقَدَّمَ مِن رَفْعه حَجَر البِئْر ومِن قَوْله لَها: امْشِي خَلْفِي
evidence.gloss: ‘The best that thou canst hire is the strong, the trustworthy’: that is, hire him for his strength and his trustworthiness. He asked her about him, and she told him of what had gone before: his lifting the stone of the well, and his saying to her, walk behind me.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Qasas 28:26, at 3277, one ayah). Opened the packet for 28:26 (all five sources) and the Jalalayn on 28:23 to 28:26. The Jalalayn on 28:26 (al-Mahalli, surah 28) glosses the strong and trustworthy as hire him for his strength and trust, then says her father asked her about him and she told him of his lifting the well’s stone (narrated at 28:24) and his telling her to walk behind him (narrated at 28:25). The sentence paraphrases exactly this; the pairing of the two deeds with strength and trust follows his sequence without adding to it. Plain sense faithful to 28:23 to 28:25 (the watering, the father’s great age, the summons). src names al-Mahalli correctly. entry-check ok, no changes.
